gaps: The stated success bar is members bringing others in unprompted, but only admins can copy or share invite links, and an invite event records a tap rather than a sent invitation or who brought in a joiner. The proposed counts cannot establish that success signal (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:12; docs/decisions/0001-mvp-small-group-india.md:18; docs/specs/circles.md:35).

The deployment configuration does not say whether it identifies the owner by Google account ID or email, or what happens to owner access after account deletion and signup again. Accounts identifies people by stable Google account ID and permits email changes, so an email-based configuration could assign or lose access incorrectly (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:23; docs/specs/accounts.md:23; docs/specs/accounts.md:126).

Events linked to members are retained for the app's lifetime, although the stated need is owner-visible counts. The spec gives no limit or justification for retaining identifiable action history after it has been counted, against the Brief's instruction to store only what is needed (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:32; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:45; docs/product/BRIEF.md:46).

The spec does not define whether 'last 7 days' and 'last 30 days' mean rolling durations or Indian Standard Time calendar dates, or the inclusive and exclusive boundaries. Both interpretations satisfy the wording but produce different counts (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:48; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:88).

New-member counts must survive deletion to remain historical, but onboarding is not one of the five retained events and account deletion removes the account and consent record. The spec does not define what durable, anonymous record supplies past-period new-member counts (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:29; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:51; docs/specs/accounts.md:117).

New-circle counts must include circles later deleted if they are historical period counts, but the spec requires preserving only their past usage events and last names. It does not require preserving their creation times, leaving past-period new-circle counts undefined after deletion (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:43; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:52; docs/specs/circles.md:119).

Per-circle search attribution is easy to misread: a search carries every circle the searcher belongs to, while its found-person count is across all circles. The spec does not state that a circle row's searches and found-nobody counts describe its members' searches and global zero-result searches, rather than matches or missing cards in that particular circle (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:37; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:56; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:26; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:48).

The counts-only and no-member-drill-down restrictions are stated for the view, but the access criterion does not explicitly prohibit returning raw member-linked event records through direct data requests, including to the owner. That leaves the data-response boundary unclear despite the stored actor and card-holder fields (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:32; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:66; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:70; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:102).
contradictions: The spec requires every WhatsApp tap event to be recorded, while the confirmed Find and contact spec requires WhatsApp to open even when event recording fails and says that tap goes uncounted. Both acceptance contracts cannot hold for that failure case (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:86; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:71).

The spec promises that, after deletion, no event can be traced back to the member, yet it retains event times and circle attribution and shows period counts for each circle. In a circle with one member or one admin, a join or invite count can identify that person's action even after member identifiers are removed; the absolute anonymity criterion is therefore not achievable as written (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:40; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:56; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:99; docs/specs/circles.md:25).
resolutions: Why now states the counts are proxies; spread is measured by joins and circles created by someone other than the owner; who-brought-whom is out of scope.
Owner is identified by Google account ID in configuration; a recreated owner account has no access until the configuration is updated.
Member and card-holder links are justified by distinct active-member and distinct-holder counts, and removed on account deletion.
Periods are defined from 00:00 IST six or 29 days before today up to the moment the view opens; all time has no start.
New members counts current accounts only; deleted accounts are not counted, so no durable onboarding record is needed.
Deleted circles keep last name, creation time and deletion, so new-circle counts include them.
Per-circle search counts are those made by the circle's members; found-nobody is across all the searcher's circles.
No request returns individual event records or member identifiers to anyone, the owner included.
A WhatsApp tap whose recording fails goes uncounted, matching Find and contact; AC2 carries the exception.
Replaced absolute untraceability with removal of member identifiers, acknowledging small-circle inference and relying on owner-only, counts-only access.

  count distinct active members and distinct card holders contacted. When a
  member deletes their account, their identity is removed from every event
  they appear in (Accounts); the events stay, carrying no member identifier.

  is why the view is owner-only and shows counts alone.

  and deletion are kept so the view can show and count it (Circles).
